contract.reader: An engineer who has followed the discrete measurement chain of the earlier entries and now meets integrated MEMS sensors in a design
contract.problem: Understanding what a MEMS sensor does internally, what limits it, and what a smart sensor's built-in processing changes for the user
contract.outcome: Explain silicon's mechanical advantages and scaling; compute an accelerometer's deflection, capacitance change and thermomechanical noise floor; explain the Coriolis gyroscope and bias drift; describe on-chip temperature compensation, self-test and digital interfaces; weigh integrated against discrete designs
contract.contribution: One representative design carried through numbers that show why the electronics must share the package (femtofarads against 100 pF of cable) and where the mechanical noise floor lies, with the user-side costs of integration made explicit
contract.evidence: Derivations and worked numbers on the page; Fraden (2016); Gabrielson (1993); Kaajakari (2009); Senturia (2001)
contract.limitations: A representative design, not product data; fabrication only at the level of the two process families; no magnetometers or environmental sensors
